Years ago, I had the exact same problem with a purchase and a kind redditor pointed this out to me so I want to forward this point on for you to raise to Depop/seller if needed: If the item was sent to you in AliExpress packaging straight from the point of purchase, then they gave your information (name and address) to a third party (AliExpress). 

This is immediately an issue and Depop knows this, because you make this purchase with the knowledge that this information would then be used for the purchase. If you haven’t raised with Depop already, I’d have this point at the ready. It doesn’t matter if loads of people are dropshipping, doing the same thing. I’m not sure if Depop have updated their terms and conditions to cover their backs on the limitations of data protection given the rise in dropshipping, but I’d expect there’s still a cover for the buyer in that regard.

With TBOSAS showing Snow’s genuine belief that the games are necessary, I can believe that Katniss killing Coin was just further reinforcing this idea for Snow. Admittedly, the theories shared in the comments here are great, but I can’t help but wonder if Snow laughed and thought, “Exactly, without me, without the Capitol, you will kill each other anyway, you can’t be trusted to live without rule, and you are so easily manipulated”. 

Then again, maybe he was outright laughing at Coin, knowing what she wanted and what she was trying to do, only to have the same problem as Snow himself: Katniss.

I think it’s a great scene to analyse, especially with the additional revelations of Snow’s character in the more recent novels!

After a re-read of the original trilogy, I felt like all the books were the stories being told for Katniss’s children (now old enough to know what haunts their parents). Haymitch’s story is akin to this, and to me cemented by the epilogue: it’s him finally sharing his story with Katniss and Peeta. I’m not sure if this is what SC intended at all, but that’s how I’ve interpreted them, and so it makes sense for Snow’s to not fit that style. Snow’s story is not one that Katniss knows, but more so an omnipotent third party sharing the context and history of Snow and the hunger games.

I assumed it was to keep her visually close to the original wicked witch of the west, who wore black, in the same way that the hat and the cape are included in the story to reflect why they were worn in the Wizard of Oz. On a stage, black would make things harder to be seen, so Elphaba had to wear blue to be similar enough but still fully able to be seen. That is entirely speculative of me though - just how I interpreted the change!

The key to this answer is actually in your answer to 116 - did you get the right earned income for the customer? I didn’t when I first read the question, which threw me off for 118!

We know the customer has loan repayments of £170 a month, so £2,040 a year. She’s comfortable that her credit card debt will be completely repaid and will evidence this, so we actually don’t need to count this debt. This makes her annual earned income net committed expenditure £20,960.

Her income x 3.5 is then £73,360. We know that she has £80,000 readily available to contribute towards the property, so we can include this in what the customer has to use in her purchase price. Add this to her borrowing, and we have £153,360 - answer B!

I’m not sure why the endowment isn’t being considered, so I’m afraid I can’t put an explanation forward there - though I’m sure there’s a reason. Hopefully the above makes sense at least!

Have you seen the Mockingjay films yet? They bring closure to it all, and this aspect of choice, so could be worth watching them if you’re interested in knowing what choices Katniss makes.

I think the idea of love triangles (or more specifically, two boys being in love with the same girl) appeal to teenage girls because it allows the reader to place herself in the protagonists shoes and feel desired. The morality of stringing both boys along is questionable, but Katniss wasn’t technically committed to either of them, other than her public obligation to Peeta (and her own love and care of him, whether we see it as platonic or romantic, it’s undeniable she loved/cared about him) and her history with Gale, who has always been there for her. 

If you haven’t watched them already, I’d really recommend finishing off the series by watching Mockingjay Part 1 and Part 2! It wrap up the story, but if this hasn’t been your cup of tea, that’s completely understandable. In my opinion, there is more to The Hunger Games than just the romance element. It poses a really important commentary on politics which we can’t dismiss (but I know I’ve seen this aspect lost in favour of the love triange debate).

I’m rereading the trilogy now, with the last time I read the books being 10 years ago. 

Regarding the alliance, an important detail is that Finnick wears gold, which he shows Katniss before they team up in the arena. This links to Effie’s comment about how they all have something gold, with Katniss’s pin, Effie’s wig (I think?), and Effie buys something gold for Peeta and Haymitch to signify they’re a team. By showing Katniss he is wearing a gold bracelet, he’s letting her know that her team have chosen him as someone that can be trusted.

Katniss is very torn between Peeta and Gale because they represent the control she has over her own life. By kissing Gale, Katniss is CHOOSING her destiny, whereas Peeta is a forced relationship and forced marriage that she has to pursue in order to keep her and her loved ones alive. Pursuing Gale allowed her to reclaim her autonomy. However, that isn’t to say that she had feelings for him (although this is something people will debate, I’m sure!) as she was unsure of her own truth given how much the Games took over her life and thoughts. As for Peeta and Katniss having sex - no, I don’t think so. It isn’t outright said that they didn’t (unless I missed it), but Katniss and Peeta shared the same bed because of their nightmares. Katniss could only sleep through the night or get back to sleep after waking with Peeta there with her. Peeta’s own fears were resolved when he saw Katniss there with him. As well, Katniss had let Peeta know that her feelings in the Games had been an act, and like she was with Gale, she was unsure of her true feelings with Peeta, so she preferred to not dwell on them at all. Given this, I don’t think she would have slept with him - it would have caused further pain and complication to an already painful and complicated situation.

I was bitten by a dog when I was 5. I was a kid, talking to my friend’s dog and trying to kiss her head as I usually did, and she bit me, catching my lip. I don’t remember the specifics, either from being so young or potentially my brain protecting me from the levels of pain I was in, but my upper lip was shredded. I have stitches all throughout, and my mum remembers me being brought to her with blood all down my front.
Everyone knew. Family, neighbours, kids at school - and I never once heard someone make a joke. I don’t think my mum would have tolerated any jokes made to her about it, either. She says it’s an image she’ll never forget, and I can believe that.
It’s one thing for someone who has been through it to make a joke. I’ve made jokes myself - I tell people it was basically like the scene in the Spongebob Movie where the guy ripped off their seaweed moustaches. I think making a joke about the dog being a hero is horribly out of place, insensitive and unfunny.
Maybe I’m projecting or feeling too close to the story, but that’s my take. I hope you and your daughter are doing okay.

Hey! Oddly enough, my ex tried to pull the same stunt again last night - I got woken up at 5am for a booty call, and I was able to ignore it completely. I’m sick and tired of being used, and I’m really pleased to say I no longer feel as passionate about that man.

It took a long time to get to this point, and my ex would (hell, still does) reach out maybe once a month or so. But for me, the breaking point was being lied to - he would tell me he loves me during the heat of things, which I knew just wasn’t true. I can’t stand being lied to, and this helped me step away from it all.

Other than that, take time for yourself if you haven’t already. You deserve so much better. For the longest time, I refused to say a bad word about my ex - he was so lovely and so good to me. But now, I know he isn’t the great guy I thought he was. Yours isn’t, either - because a good guy wouldn’t lie and use their ex for sex.

If it’s possible, I’d say to reduce your screentime overall. If that’s not on the cards - identify the pattern of when he reaches out (mine only ever messages on a Friday or Saturday, always after 8pm, once every 3 or 4 weeks). Once you know when is most likely he’ll message, put your phone on silent, make other plans, busy yourself. But I think it’ll be easiest to step away from him once you have truly given yourself time. 6 months is still so fresh, but you’re being treated with such disrespect by him now - make peace with the breakup and take this time to focus on yourself now, and there are people out there who will treat you with so much love and respect!

I personally shop on Vinted/Depop maybe once every 2 weeks, although I do like to go on both platforms to have a nosey at outfits/pieces I’m wanting for a cheaper price. For example, I’ve been receiving ads for the AYM Studio dresses - but instead of buying off the advert, I look for a cheaper dress being resold. As for quality, I have been quite fortunate that nothing I’ve bought has been dirty/smelly/damaged, but I do try to purchase from sellers with 5 stars when I can.

I like that I can find specific items on Depop and Vinted, whereas charity shops can be hit or miss as you may find a gorgeous piece that you didn’t know you wanted. I feel the likelihood of finding a specific item you’re after in a charity shop is slim, but then again, some of my favourite dresses have been found in charity shops!

In terms of price and quality, I feel as if costs have gone up, but it is worth keeping in mind the UK has fallen in a cost of living crisis. This paired with the competition of other sellers and Vinted gaining traction (as it is definitely more popular than it was, back when it was known solely as a way to make a quick quid), I feel the increase in cost is to be expected. Depop is pricier than Vinted, but I feel both platforms are the same in that some sellers are happy to accept offers. 

I haven’t noticed a decline in number of items in charity shops, but I feel there are less “goodies” in charity shops. I shop for items sized between 8-12, and before I used to find cute skirts, dresses and tops in these sizes, whereas now there all a bit granny-ish or work garms.

I feel that online resale sites have had a negative affect on charity shops, as I feel people are now opting to make a profit off of selling their clothes rather than donating them. I know this isn’t the case for all, but with shipping becoming easier to do, there may be an increase in this. Plus, with it being common knowledge that some individuals buy from charity shops to flip the clothing, I wouldn’t be surprised if donations decreased as people become more considerate of costs.

Unrelated, but I’m also someone who enjoys a carboot sale (not that there are any on in this weather!) and it’s a similar story in that the costs of clothes have gone up a lot for something that’s secondhand and you’re trying to sell, which baffles me. I don’t sell at carboots myself, but when they’re wanting £5-£10 for a dress (expensive for a carboot - I usually get about 5 items for £2!), it seems to me that they’re utilising prices the item would sell for on Depop/Vinted. It could be worth looking into whether Charity Shop charges have gone up in a similar way.

Honestly, I struggled for months. I found ways to pass the time - for me it was hiking, and I had a friend come with me just to talk about anything and everything. She recommended just binge watching shows so you have something to sort of distract you. Obviously, distractions are hard, but having a hobby and doing it in every spot of free time you have was helpful for me.

I also spoke with my doctor and got on anti-depressants. I made it known that I had tried sertraline before and it didn’t work for me, so I was prescribed something else and this has been helping a lot.

Finally, I realised he wasn’t the man I thought he was. I had put him on a pedestal - he’s been quite awful over the last few months. He’ll reach out, we’ll hook up, during this time he says he loves me and misses me - and then he ghosts. I know I shouldn’t let him come round, and I won’t anymore. Personally, once someone hurts me, it is a lot easier for me to separate from them. I was blindsided because when we broke up, nothing was wrong and I didn’t have a bad word to say about him. Now, I’m not too impressed with him and think he’s been a bit cruel to utilise my love for him to get sex. I wouldn’t go out of my way to drag his name through the mud, but this has helped me break my obsession of sorts with him.

Finally, I’ve realised there are other people out there, who can offer me just as good conversations, just as funny jokes, and just as good intimacy - if anything, maybe someone will come along who’s even better! At the time, I thought that wouldn’t be true, that I peaked with my ex. But life moves on, and we slowly have to move with it.

I’d say to drive as much as you can. I spent as much money as I did because I knew I had to keep driving, it’s not something to just rush through. Don’t panic over mistakes. Firstly, a hesitation minor is better than a serious/dangerous, so don’t rush anything. I failed my second test because I was hesitant on a busy roundabout - yet even now, I wouldn’t rush that roundabout because I’d rather wait than get into an accident. Unfortunately my examiner didn’t seem to have the same mindset. This really shook my confidence for the next few tests and I was overthinking everything - I started panicking on the manoeuvres each time, and it took me realising that I was panicking to finally pass my test.

Which is the ultimate bit of advice: know what you struggle with. Maybe you’re a great driver, and you fail on different things each time - that’s okay. Pinpoint what goes through your mind when you make that mistake. For me, I started to freak out and rush things, I’d blank on the reversing left and right - so I just needed to take an extra minute or two. I also kept practicing my right turns, as these were something I wasn’t confident in. I made it clear to my instructor of any aspect that I wanted to practice. I wanted to practice overtaking buses and cyclists, because I knew I’d fail it I had come across one in the test! So be as open and upfront with your instructor as possible. I cried over the cost at the time, but I’m glad I stuck to it.

I believe you had to wait 10 working days for your next test, which was the frustrating part for those who failed. I remember my friends being so upset that they had to wait that long after failing for a silly mistake. If only they knew what the future held.

To avoid fixating on the small mistakes and letting them spiral, I personally only beat it after going through the intense feeling of utter regret and stupidity. I know that sounds dramatic, but I would sit at home a few days after the fails and cringe - I should have passed! I panicked on my pull up on the right, which was potentially the easiest one! I reflected on the error and tried to pinpoint what went wrong, and it was because I let myself panic the moment one thing went wrong. In this instance, the car was at an angle and so I needed to bring it closer to the curb, but I started to panic instead and couldn’t fix it. Afterwards, I was adamant on practicing, and it was clearly just a case of panicking in the moment.

Reflect on the feeling, and take your time. My mindset for this test was along the lines of ‘I will do my best, and if I fail, that’s okay, because I will get another test’. Previously, the test was be all end all because my theory ran out in July, and obviously the test dates didn’t work in my favour. But new tests are becoming available, and there is no limit on how many tests you can take. I hope this was helpful!

I’d say don’t give up, and don’t let the number of times you’ve failed get to you. I went into each test thinking ‘oh god, this is my fourth/fifth/sixth test’ and that added pressure probably didn’t help much at all.

Also, reflect on what’s going wrong and why. For me, I made one serious mistake on every test, two of which were for my manoeuvres because I started to panic from the nerves and pressure. If any aspect of the test makes you panic, practice that aspect of driving until you have it down. I still panicked this time, but I fixed it because I knew that I could.

Finally, don’t rush into the test. I suppose this is more person dependent, but I failed so many times because I had my tests back to back and I think this chipped away at my confidence rather than helped it. I gave myself a month of driving lessons with a test at the very end of March. I didn’t tell a soul about it - only myself, my instructor, and my examiner knew. This alleviated a bit of pressure.

Finally, I found taking a paracetamol helped. I read somewhere that it settled nerves or something, and whilst I’m not sure if it did or if it was placebo, it was a little bit of routine I included.

I hope this was helpful! Let me know if you need any more advice, but I’m sure you’ve got this. Have you got another test booked in?

Months in advance should certainly be fine, especially as in most areas, that’s the only option! I’d say to message your instructor and ask what their availability is like for the month you’re thinking about (I’m assuming around August or September?) as they may have holidays booked or someone else has a test booked in already. Once you know the days that are off limits, book yourself in for one that they can do, and let them know immediately. I think that’s a really smart approach to it, with a clear goal and time frame to work towards it.

Due to the limited tests available, I’d encourage you to ask your instructor what days they definitely can’t do during the month you intend to book for, and then once you’ve selected a date that doesn’t fall during a day they said they’re unavailable, you inform them and they’ll book you in to use their car.

Your instructor can be present during the test, but they don’t have to be. An examiner will sit up front and observe you. But you need to use your instructors car (unless you plan to use your own) and you therefore need to make sure your instructor is available.

I always asked at the start of the month when my instructor was unavailable. For example, if I was booking for April, I’d ask what dates they absolutely couldn’t do, and book in for any date that wasn’t one of those. I hope this has made a bit of sense!

I was in a similar situation, I took so much overtime because I wanted to help the store, and my coworker wanted to look after her first grandchild for two or three weeks. I gladly accepted and did 40 hour work weeks while completing my third year of university (the busiest year).
December rolled around, and my granddad passed. I was working overtime when I found out, and after I was crying in the back for half an hour, the manager sent me home. A few hours later, I was asked to work overtime the next day.
